subject: Anthropology
title: Colonialism and Resistance
description: A quick win: understand Colonialism and Resistance.

hook.text: Colonial subjects weren't passive victims. From armed revolts to cultural revival, resistance took countless forms.

buildup.text: Colonized peoples resisted through armed rebellion, religious movements, cultural revival, and quiet daily acts.

discovery.text: Anticolonial leaders like Fanon argued that colonialism damages the mind. Liberation requires mental decolonization too.

twist.text: Resistance also came from within colonial systems. Interpreters, clerks, and teachers subverted power from the inside.

climax.text: Colonial resistance shows that domination always produces opposition. Power never flows one way for long.

quiz.question: What did Fanon argue about colonialism?
options: Liberation requires mental decolonization as well as political freedom

details.summary: Colonial rule imposed European political systems on colonized peoples, disrupting indigenous governance through indirect rule, forced labor, and administrative boundaries that ignored existing political structures. Resistance took forms from armed rebellion to everyday non-compliance.
details.whyItMatters: Colonialism's political legacy shapes the modern world — most contemporary states were created by colonial boundaries. Understanding colonial governance and resistance explains ongoing political instability, ethnic conflict.
takeaways: Colonialism imposed European political systems on indigenous societies
Colonial boundaries ignored existing political and ethnic structures
Resistance ranged from armed rebellion to everyday non-compliance

faq.question: What was indirect rule?
faq.answer: Colonial powers (especially Britain) governed through existing local leaders, co-opting chiefs and kings into colonial administration. This was cheaper than direct rule but distorted indigenous authority structures — leaders became accountable to colonial governments rather than their own.

faq.question: How did colonized peoples resist?
faq.answer: Through armed rebellions, political movements, cultural revitalization, refusal to comply with labor demands, hidden transcripts of resistance, and strategic manipulation of colonial systems. Resistance was constant, creative, and far more widespread than colonial archives typically recorded.
